A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new method that allows to improve the performance of video ReID by fusing appearance and motion information from image and optical flow streams.
we propose to use Mutual Attention network for fusion of image appearance and motion features, and we also introduce a method to use longer input sequences for better representation.

the proposed method is a general purpose framework that is applicable to any 2D backbone network, and it can be extended to other video analytics tasks such as person re-identification and action recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed Mutual Attention module is generic and can be applied to any CNN architecture for video based ReID.
the motion information can provide additional discriminant cues for person ReID.
a flow guided mutual attention network can be easily incorporated into any 2D backbone to learn discriminant video level representations for person ReID.
